key_insight: A reverse-diode effect explains the S-shaped current-voltage behavior in valley photovoltaic devices and links their poor electrical performance to inefficient electron extraction.
engineering_relevance: The equivalent-circuit framework provides a practical diagnostic tool for identifying and removing transport barriers that must be fixed before valley photovoltaics can reach high efficiency.
method: Measured intensity- and voltage-dependent photoluminescence alongside electrical responses.
Built an equivalent-circuit model to jointly fit PL and I-V behavior, including the S-shape.
Used Poisson/drift-diffusion simulations to test whether the reverse diode arises from valley scattering or a heterojunction barrier.
evidence_signal: The model simultaneously reproduces photoluminescence and electrical measurements, including the previously observed S-shaped current-voltage curves.
watch_item: The analysis shows that device performance is limited until the reverse-diode mechanism is eliminated, whether it originates from intrinsic valley scattering or an interfacial barrier.
paper_title: Combined photoluminescence and electrical characterization of valley photovoltaic devices explained with an equivalent circuit
